amendment.rationale: No requirement meaning changed. A frozen controller policy defect prevented safe absent-file sidecar preparation; repair only that validator condition and regression tests. Because no product implementation or accepted phase exists, the blocked full draft remains the unimplemented impact closure, and its exact intended writes/all53unchanged obligations must be prepared under the corrected freeze. Preserve previous blocked run and all contract/generated identities.

change_summary: Developer-authorized narrow controller-policy correction permits absent implementation files represented by task sidecars, preserving all requirements, selected Todo behavior, dependencies, canonical contracts and generated bytes; then resume full preparation.

scenarios.description: Fixture: absent application-data profile on the supported Mac, runtime networking blocked. Launch the delivered package, use its create action, exit normally and launch the same profile again. Oracle: profile identity, empty task set and default-view controls recorded independently. Evidence: packaged journey, profile manifest and screenshots.
scenarios.expected: Both launches reach usable Open/Any/empty-search/newest-created views of the same initially empty collection; no service credentials are requested and creation is available.

scenarios.description: Fixture: acknowledged Open and Completed records, duplicate content, absent/present dates, Unicode text and a clock-corrected history whose updated time precedes completed time. Exit with no pending operation and relaunch. Oracle: independent acknowledgment ledger containing every field and identity; do not derive expected records from storage reads. Evidence: before/after semantic records.
scenarios.expected: Every stored identity, title, notes, due date, status and all three timestamp fields equals the ledger; no record is dropped, rewritten or incorrectly restamped.

scenarios.description: Fixture: empty collection and controlled UTC clock. Submit a valid title with outer Unicode whitespace, CRLF/CR notes and a date, wait for acknowledgment, then deliberately submit identical input again. Oracle: explicit normalized text constants, two distinct canonical IDs and initially equal created/updated instants. Evidence: command outcomes, visible task set and reopened state.
scenarios.expected: Each deliberate submission creates exactly one Open task with no completed time. Normalized values are stored, initial timestamps agree, and the two opaque identities differ.

scenarios.description: Fixture: independent vectors with 1 and 200-scalar normalized titles, empty and 10000-scalar normalized notes, Unicode combining sequences, valid dates 0001-01-01/2000-02-29/2028-02-29/9999-12-31, and both valid statuses in a backup. Exercise create, edit and restore with the same applicable vectors. Oracle: scalar counts and normalized constants generated independently of product validators. Evidence: boundary responses and semantic snapshots.
scenarios.expected: All exactly valid boundary values succeed without truncation. Title trim and CRLF/CR-to-LF notes normalization are consistent at all entry boundaries; valid history permits clock corrections.

scenarios.description: Fixture: two identical-content tasks, one Completed with a known completed instant. Edit title, notes and due date independently; clear notes/date; also edit the Completed task. Restart after acknowledgment. Oracle: expected per-ID records, with immutable identity/created/status/completed fields marked explicitly. Evidence: command responses and reopened records.
scenarios.expected: Only the selected identity changes its content. Optional fields can be cleared. Created time and status remain unchanged; editing Completed retains its completed instant. Changed content updates updated time.

scenarios.description: Fixture: changed create draft and changed existing-task editor, including invalid entered values. For each of task switch, another create, cancel, restore initiation and normal close, attempt the action and choose retain, then repeat choosing discard. Oracle: exact raw editor values and preexisting committed-record snapshot. Evidence: dialog/focus journey and database snapshot.
scenarios.expected: Retain cancels the attempted navigation and preserves exact input for correction. Explicit discard permits navigation while leaving committed task data unchanged. No draft is exported or treated as committed.

scenarios.description: Fixture: Open task due yesterday and an unaffected twin; controlled completion clock. Complete the selected task, inspect Open and Completed views, then repeat the explicit set-Completed request with a different clock value. Oracle: exact records and view identity sets. Evidence: responses, view snapshots and restart.
scenarios.expected: First transition preserves content/identity/created, sets completed and updated to the completion instant, removes the task from Open and adds it to Completed. Repeated set-Completed changes neither data nor timestamps.

scenarios.description: Fixture: Completed task due yesterday with known timestamps and fixed Today. Reopen, inspect status/date views, then repeat explicit set-Open with a different clock value. Oracle: expected task and identity sets. Evidence: responses, visible results and restart.
scenarios.expected: Reopening preserves content/identity/created, clears completed time, sets updated time and recalculates Overdue. Repeated set-Open has no additional effect or timestamp change.

scenarios.description: Fixture: two identical-content tasks and a backup captured before deletion. Cancel deletion of one, then confirm its prompt and restart; export again. Oracle: selected identity and independent before/after task sets. Evidence: identifying permanent-deletion prompt, persisted set and both backup documents.
scenarios.expected: Cancel changes nothing. Confirmation removes only the selected identity from every view and the new backup; the twin remains. The old backup may retain the deleted identity, and the prompt states deletion is permanent.

scenarios.description: Fixture Q1 is defined in functional-analysis.md with explicit identities/fields. Inspect Open, Completed and All with selected search/date constraints; open each notes editor. Change all query preferences, exit and relaunch. Oracle: the authored Q1 set table, not the product query evaluator. Evidence: identity sets, row semantics and launch controls.
scenarios.expected: Visible IDs equal the requested status AND search AND date set. Each row exposes title, status and present due date plus notes inspection/edit. Every relaunch resets Open, Any date, empty search and newest-created ordering.

scenarios.description: Fixture Q1 at Today=2028-02-29. Exercise all 3 status views x 4 date filters with empty, one-match and no-match search. Oracle: independent authored truth table, including All/Overdue={01}, All/Today={02,03,08}, All/NoDate={05,07,0a}, Completed/Overdue={}. Evidence: exact visible sets/counts.
scenarios.expected: Any adds no date predicate; Today includes dated Open and Completed tasks; Overdue includes only Open tasks before Today; NoDate includes only absent dates. Constraints combine with logical AND.

scenarios.description: Fixture Q1 and isolated folding vectors; use empty and outer-Unicode-whitespace queries, STRASSE, café versus cafe, decomposed éclair, notes-only needle, literal [a.*%_], Greek sigma forms and non-Turkic I/dotless-I/dotted-I vectors. Oracle: frozen normalized/folded comparison constants and explicit ID sets. Snapshot stored text before/after. Evidence: query results and untouched semantic records.
scenarios.expected: Empty trimmed query adds no restriction. NFC then default full non-Turkic fold finds case/canonical equivalents and notes-only matches, preserves diacritic significance and treats punctuation as literal. Stored text is never rewritten.

scenarios.description: Fixture Q1 includes tied created instants, tied due dates and missing dates. Query all three orderings, then repeat after restart and on status/date/search subsets. Oracle: authored ordered ID lists in functional-analysis.md. Evidence: complete visible order, not just first/last rows.
scenarios.expected: Newest/oldest use created descending/ascending followed by canonical identity ascending. Earliest due uses dates ascending with absent last, then created descending and identity ascending; ties are stable in every view.

scenarios.description: Fixture: empty profile then Q1. Inspect empty collection, no-match query and nonempty matches; create/edit/complete/reopen/delete/restore records that change membership. Oracle: independent resulting identity sets and counts after each acknowledged action. Evidence: count/state text and clear-controls journey.
scenarios.expected: Count equals the matching set after every successful change. Empty collection offers create; nonempty collection with zero matches offers clear search/filters. Clearing constraints returns the correct default-compatible results.

scenarios.description: Fixture: controlled local calendar at 2028-02-28, 2028-02-29 and 2028-03-01, Open/Completed tasks on each date, and zone changes that cross a date boundary. Exercise active midnight/leap-day/zone transitions and suspend/resume/focus after a transition. Oracle: authored sets at each local date and monotonic deadline measurements. Evidence: timed visible result changes plus unchanged stored date snapshot.
scenarios.expected: Active Today/Overdue results refresh within 60 seconds; resume or focus refreshes within one second. Stored due dates never change and Completed tasks never become Overdue.

scenarios.description: Fixture: deterministic barriers before transaction commit and after commit before reply. Exercise create/edit/complete/reopen/delete/restore. Pause each operation before commit, inspect UI and independent store; release and wait for acknowledgment. Oracle: commit checkpoint, independent acknowledgment ledger and exact old/new states. Evidence: checkpoint trace and UI states.
scenarios.expected: UI reports pending while persistence is unresolved; no saved-success claim precedes commit. After acknowledged commit the correct results appear. Any optimistic content remains visibly pending until acknowledgment.

scenarios.description: Fixture: rejected-before-commit write and a lost reply after possible commit, with separately exercised wholly-present and wholly-absent outcomes. Preserve exact submitted input and generated attempt identity. Attempt retry before reconciliation, then after an authoritative outcome. Oracle: ledger, receipt/attempt correlation and semantic store state. Evidence: actionable messages and retry-gate trace.
scenarios.expected: Confirmed rejection leaves old committed state and permits correction/retry. Unknown outcome is neither success nor confirmed failure; conflicting/duplicate-capable retry stays blocked until reconciled. Available input survives and messages contain neither raw SQL nor stack traces.

scenarios.description: Fixture: delayed create and delayed set-status, plus another selected task. Rapidly repeat the initiating action; try conflicting edit/delete/restore and use search/views/focus while pending. Request normal close before outcome. After resolution perform a deliberate identical-content create. Oracle: native admission/effect counts and independent task ledger. Evidence: pending controls, responsive journey and close timeline.
scenarios.expected: One pending task mutation/restore is admitted and repeated activation has one effect. Conflicting mutations remain unavailable until resolved; viewing/search work. Normal close displays waiting and awaits outcome without discarding submitted input. Later deliberate create may create a distinct task.

scenarios.description: Fixture: Q1 plus an unsubmitted draft and restrictive active filters. Export to selected local SSD file, exit source package, restore that file into a fresh profile on the same supported Mac. Oracle: independent full committed-field ledger and parsed versioned UTF-8 JSON document. Evidence: saved location, unencrypted-data UI notice and independent fresh-profile records.
scenarios.expected: Export includes every committed identity and required field in one consistent snapshot, disregards filters and excludes drafts. Round trip preserves field meaning and identity independently of source database. Today/Overdue are recomputed, not authoritative backup fields.

scenarios.description: Fixture: existing sentinel destination file and a new destination on qualified local SSD. Cancel overwrite, then confirm export, injecting failure before publication and interruption at publication boundaries. Oracle: old-file digest and complete parsed new backup digest; saved location. Evidence: permission/overwrite journey and reconciled filesystem state.
scenarios.expected: Existing file changes only after explicit replacement confirmation, and then only to a complete valid backup. Cancellation/confirmed prepublication failure preserve it. Uncertain publication leaves whole old or whole new; outcome reconciles before retry. New incomplete file is never called complete.

scenarios.description: Fixture: full valid backup, valid empty backup, and one defective record located last in an otherwise valid 10000-record backup. Validate before offering restore confirmation. Oracle: independent full-document validity vectors and current collection/source-file digests. Evidence: candidate summary/error and unchanged digests.
scenarios.expected: Every record/document condition is validated before replacement is offered. Valid empty backup is accepted. A defect anywhere rejects the candidate, identifies its record or document condition, and changes neither source file nor collection.

scenarios.description: Fixture: existing collection A of 3 tasks, validated file B of 2 tasks and a changed editor draft. Initiate restore, retain draft once, then explicitly discard and inspect/cancel confirmation; repeat and confirm. Oracle: candidate identity and exact A/B counts. Evidence: dialog text, draft journey and cancellation snapshot.
scenarios.expected: Draft protection occurs before discard. Confirmation identifies selected file and both counts, states entire-collection replacement rather than merge, and requires explicit action. Cancellation preserves A. Only the confirmed validated candidate becomes eligible to apply.

scenarios.description: Fixture: disjoint collections A and B with different identities/content, including a Completed clock-corrected record. Validate B, then change source-file bytes to C while retaining native candidate B; confirm B. Repeat restore with deterministic process cuts. Oracle: independently authored A/B/C ledgers, candidate token and default-view set. Evidence: semantic records and recovery states.
scenarios.expected: Successful restore contains exactly B with its original required values/timestamps, resets default view and does not merge or restamp history. Source changes cannot substitute C: use retained B or renew validation/confirmation. Interruption yields whole A or whole B.

scenarios.description: Fixture: delivered package/profile with changed unsubmitted draft; sequential second launch then repeated simultaneous launches. Observe processes, collection ownership and windows before/after. Oracle: permitted one database owner and exact draft values. Evidence: process/window trace and draft screenshot.
scenarios.expected: One usable collection window and at most one database-owning application process exist. The existing window activates, extra launches exit before becoming writers and the existing draft remains intact.

scenarios.description: Fixture: installed release package with network access blocked and no runtime development tools. Open local help and application identity using keyboard. Oracle: required topics and release evidence version/package digest. Evidence: displayed help/version and functional journey.
scenarios.expected: Offline help explains task operations, local date semantics, data/backup locations, whole replacement on restore, permanent deletion without built-in undo and old backups retaining deleted tasks. Displayed version matches the installed release.

scenarios.description: Fixture: empty/Unicode-whitespace title, 201-scalar title, internal LF/CR/VT/FF/NEL/LS/PS, NUL in title/notes, 10001-scalar normalized notes, invalid Gregorian dates including 1900-02-29, year 0000/10000, malformed YYYY-MM-DD, unknown status, Open with completed time and Completed without completed time. Submit through UI and direct native boundary, then import backups. Oracle: independently authored validity matrix and old-state digest. Evidence: typed errors/raw draft retention.
scenarios.expected: Every invalid vector is rejected before state change, without truncation. Errors identify field/capacity or backup record/document condition; editable values remain for correction. Backup source bytes remain unchanged.

scenarios.description: Fixture: exactly 200 scalar title using 100 decomposed e+combining-accent pairs, 201-scalar counterpart, multiscalar emoji sequences, internal tabs/spaces, Unicode trim boundaries, notes with 10000 CRLF pairs and CR-only lines. Exercise native create/edit and candidate validation. Oracle: authored post-normalization scalars and exact text byte constants. Evidence: persisted text and rejection responses.
scenarios.expected: Limits count Unicode scalar values after only required trim/line-ending normalization. Combining/emoji text is not counted as graphemes/bytes. Internal title whitespace and other notes whitespace remain intact; storage performs no search normalization.

scenarios.description: Fixture: independently authored 9999, 10000 and 10001-record collections, with valid maximum-length fields for the capacity correctness run and mixed statuses. Create at 9999 and 10000, delete at 10000 then create, and validate/apply restore candidates at each size. Oracle: exact ID ledger and count including Completed records. Evidence: snapshots and capacity errors.
scenarios.expected: 9999->10000 creation succeeds; further creation and 10001-record restore reject without loss. Deleting one permits another create. 10000 valid maximum-length records round trip successfully; capacity is not restricted to Open tasks.

scenarios.description: Fixture: controlled clock, normalized content already stored, Completed record with completed time later than a subsequent legitimate edit instant. Save equivalent trimmed/line-ending-normalized values and repeat explicit set-status; then edit under backward clock and export/restore. Oracle: exact old/new timestamps and sort list. Evidence: operation results and semantic records.
scenarios.expected: Normalization-identical save and idempotent status set preserve updated/completed values. Actual changed content records its current UTC instant even when earlier than prior timestamps. Restore accepts that history; deterministic created-time/ID ordering still holds.

scenarios.description: Fixture Q1 with controlled asynchronous query completion. Issue query A, then B; complete B before A. Repeat while a mutation is pending and after its commit, including a calendar change. Oracle: latest active constraints, current committed revision and explicit expected IDs/count/order. Evidence: request/reply sequence and visible set.
scenarios.expected: Late results cannot replace results for newer active constraints or an acknowledged newer collection revision. Viewing remains available during writes; each settled result/count/order corresponds to one committed snapshot and the currently requested calendar/query state.

scenarios.description: Fixture: editor with exact changed/invalid input on a task subsequently hidden by search/status/date changes. Use query controls during a delayed unrelated mutation, and cause a date-dependent row to leave results. Oracle: pinned editor identity and raw draft values. Evidence: visible query results plus editor state.
scenarios.expected: Changing the result set never silently discards input. Editor remains associated with its selected identity or invokes draft protection before removal; unrelated pending operations and calendar refresh do not replace the draft.

scenarios.description: Fixture Q1 with an injected read/query failure and delayed read recovery while a task mutation is unresolved. Oracle: last valid committed snapshot and explicitly failed latest query request. Evidence: actionable error, visible loading/failure states and subsequent successful set.
scenarios.expected: A read failure is not displayed as a valid empty/no-results collection or success. User can retry, view/focus/window controls remain responsive, drafts survive and eventual successful query restores correct IDs/count/order.

scenarios.description: Fixture documents: malformed/truncated JSON, invalid UTF-8, unsupported/absent version, missing required fields, wrong field types, duplicate JSON members where candidate semantics would be ambiguous, duplicate task IDs, malformed canonical IDs/timestamps, inconsistent status/completion, invalid date/text and 10001 tasks. Include early and final defective records. Oracle: authored document/record errors and original digests. Evidence: typed validation errors.
scenarios.expected: Invalid full candidates never reach replacement confirmation. Collection/source remain unchanged and errors identify a record or document condition. Unknown format/version is rejected; no partial record import, silent truncation or defaulting required data.

scenarios.description: Fixture: disjoint pre/post mutation states, paused create/edit/delete/restore transaction, export admitted during that pause and another export request. Oracle: independently authored pre/post full ledgers and one-export admission trace. Evidence: parsed backups and operation sequencing.
scenarios.expected: Each export is exactly one complete committed snapshot, wholly before or after the write, never mixed and never including a draft/pending overlay. Export jobs are separately serialized; they do not admit a second task mutation or weaken restore exclusion.

scenarios.description: Fixture: selected destination paths equal or alias application database/recovery/migration/diagnostic files, including normalized path, symlink and hard-link aliases where supported; one selected file in an otherwise unselected directory. Oracle: protected file identities/digests and granted exact selection scope. Evidence: destination rejection and denied unrelated access.
scenarios.expected: Every protected-file alias rejects before modification. Selecting one import/export file does not permit arbitrary sibling access. Protected data and previous destination bytes remain intact.

scenarios.description: Fixture: destination/storage incapable of qualified same-directory complete atomic replacement, denied write, exhausted space, failed serialization/sync/rename and interruption around publication. Test existing sentinel and new destination. Oracle: old/new complete document digests and publication checkpoints. Evidence: filesystem outcomes and messages.
scenarios.expected: Unsupported guarantee rejects before changing an existing file. Confirmed prepublication failures preserve it; uncertain publication leaves complete old/new and reconciles before retry. A new incomplete destination is not announced successful; completion identifies the actual saved location.

scenarios.description: Fixture: nonempty A, valid empty candidate E, changed draft and selected source file changed/deleted after validation. Cancel draft prompt/confirmation; then confirm retained E. Oracle: retained candidate token/digest and exact counts, A/E ledgers. Evidence: prompts and stored state.
scenarios.expected: Cancellation preserves A and retained draft as chosen. Confirmed empty restore atomically empties the collection and offers create with default controls. A changed/deleted source cannot silently substitute content; retained validated candidate or renewed confirmation is required.

scenarios.description: Fixture: actual embedded local Turso on the supported Mac, independently reset task datasets and acknowledgment ledger. For create/edit/complete/reopen/delete, force process termination before commit, while commit is pending and after acknowledgment, 20 repetitions per operation/cut. Deterministic checkpoints make each cut meaningful; OS/filesystem/device remain functioning. Evidence: raw cut logs, ledgers and reopened full records.
scenarios.expected: Reopened state is a valid sequential history containing every acknowledged operation, with later effects allowed to supersede earlier ones. The terminal unacknowledged operation is wholly present/absent; no mixed fields, duplicate create or loss of unrelated earlier commits.

scenarios.description: Fixture: disjoint actual-Turso collections A/B and independent acknowledgment ledger. Force termination before restore commit, while commit is pending and after acknowledgment, 20 repetitions per cut on supported Mac. Reopen from disk after each cut. Evidence: deterministic checkpoint logs and independent semantic comparison.
scenarios.expected: Each reopened collection is wholly A or B, never merged. Acknowledged restore must appear in the valid history, subject only to later superseding operations; unacknowledged terminal restore may be wholly present/absent.

scenarios.description: Fixture: existing read-only, denied-permission, corrupt/invalid-file and unknown-newer-format storage; version-one storage fixture. Record original file digests/metadata before launch and retry. Oracle: unchanged available original artifacts and no successful normal mutation. Evidence: error/retry/exit journey and filesystem snapshots.
scenarios.expected: Inaccessible existing data is not first launch. Normal modification stops and actionable retry/exit appears; originals remain available. No empty replacement, deletion, automatic corruption repair or downgrade occurs. Release one rejects future versions; prior-release migration is inapplicable.

scenarios.description: Fixture: actual Turso, prior acknowledged task A and staged edit/status/delete/restore to B. Inject validation/storage failure at transaction entry, after partial statements but before commit and at a confirmed rejected commit. Oracle: independent full previous ledger and transaction result. Evidence: snapshots, errors and successful subsequent retry.
scenarios.expected: Confirmed rejection leaves full previous committed state without rolling back unrelated earlier commits. No task mixes old/new fields and restore exposes no mixed collection. Input/candidate remains available for correction or safe retry.

scenarios.description: Fixture: pending mutation with submitted input and separate unsubmitted-draft case, then concurrent second launches while existing process is pending, closing or showing a draft prompt. Oracle: one owner, pending outcome and exact input snapshots. Evidence: process/window/close traces.
scenarios.expected: Normal close waits for submitted operation outcome; it does not invoke discard as if submission were an unsubmitted draft. Changed unsubmitted input receives retain/discard protection. Additional launches never create another writer or lose existing input.

scenarios.description: Fixture: operation deliberately remains pending beyond 500 ms in packaged or explicitly identified instrumented same-revision application. Exercise query, focus and window interactions during delay; also expose success/rejection/uncertainty endings. Oracle: monotonic times and accessibility state capture. Evidence: event timeline and visible/accessibility tree.
scenarios.expected: Accessible busy feedback appears within 500 ms; focus/window interactions respond within 250 ms. Viewing works, conflicting mutation controls stay unavailable and eventual outcome removes or updates pending state correctly.

scenarios.description: Fixture: exact delivered source, Cargo metadata and package resource inventory. Stimulus: inspect every first-party production owner and Rust/WASM UI callsite; classify generated interop and test/build tooling separately. Oracle: frozen owner and dependency allowlists. Evidence: path-to-purpose inventory, Rust toolchain identity and reviewer source references.
scenarios.expected: All first-party business rules, native operations, persistence and UI state/events are Rust on the pinned stable toolchain; declarative assets and generated interop contain no first-party application behavior.

scenarios.description: Fixture: delivered ad-hoc-signed arm64 .app on REF-MAC-M3MAX in a clean authorized account/data profile. Stimulus: install/copy to the user Applications location and exercise native journeys with developer tools unavailable in the application process environment. Oracle: Tauri 2 locked dependency/runtime inventory and independent expected collection. Evidence: install transcript, package/signature/resource digests, process environment and native journey results.
scenarios.expected: The actual Tauri 2 package launches and operates without Rust compiler, dev server, Turso CLI, database service, service credentials or administrator privileges for normal use; standalone-browser results do not satisfy this scenario.

scenarios.description: Fixture: fresh actual embedded-turso store in the current account and an independent task-field ledger. Stimulus: packaged create/edit/status/delete/restore, normal exit and restart; inspect locked dependency, adapter and real opened store. Oracle: ledger replay and semantic backup decode independent of production database/query helpers. Evidence: engine version, disk artifacts and exact field/identity comparison.
scenarios.expected: The persistent local turso crate is authoritative and survives restart; no libsql substitution, browser or in-memory-only store, remote primary, cloud token/account or server is required.

scenarios.description: Fixture: clean checkout and committed toolchain/dependency/generator locks, dependency qualification packet, reference-host inventory. Stimulus: locked native and Rust/WASM builds, generated contract proof, local API call and reference-Mac .app packaging using recorded prerequisites. Oracle: exact approved versions/inventories. Evidence: commands, lock digests, build/package/API results and tool versions; dependency updates rerun affected qualification.
scenarios.expected: Pinned compatible versions reproduce all compilation units and actual packaged local API transport before contract freeze. Missing tools, unqualified generator/runtime/frontend combinations or unavailable required host evidence are unresolved rather than passes.

scenarios.description: Fixture: frozen Protobuf inventory, generated Rust traits/messages, actual service providers, typed UI transport and registered custom commands. Stimulus: real contracts check, provider/consumer compilation and C-ARCH; run checker self-fixtures inserting forbidden dependencies, unregistered calls, direct UI SQL/filesystem access and trait/signature bypasses. Oracle: frozen inventories, module allowlist and exact approved call graph. Evidence: source-referenced provider/consumer proof and expected checker rejections.
scenarios.expected: Every specified module/local API boundary consumes generated shapes/signatures in real adapters; checker fixtures fail for bypasses. UI task access uses only approved native API and cannot directly access SQL/database/arbitrary files; generated files alone are insufficient proof.

scenarios.description: Fixture: production source and direct dependency graph at the delivered revision. Stimulus: independent ownership/purpose and rule-duplication review plus unused-dependency/source inventory. Oracle: accepted requirements and frozen owners. Evidence: each module/direct dependency mapped to requirement/enabling purpose and concrete authoritative rule callsites.
scenarios.expected: No speculative or unused production feature/dependency, duplicate invariant owner, unexplained wrapper/trait/crate or unreferenced public API remains. Feedback-only UI validation is native-authoritative and its consistency is tested; generated mappings have explicit purposes.

scenarios.description: Fixture: delivered installed package, D1-derived collection and selected backup destination on the local SSD. Stimulus: block runtime networking and execute create, edit, complete, reopen, delete, all search/filter/order controls, export, fresh-profile restore, normal restart and help. Oracle: independent lifecycle/query/round-trip expectations. Evidence: isolation policy, full journey transcript, package identity and field comparisons.
scenarios.expected: Every in-scope operation succeeds under blocked runtime network without credentials or remote resources. Installation prerequisites are separate from this installed-package runtime workload.

scenarios.description: Fixture: delivered package and the complete acceptance workload. Stimulus: start qualified process-attributed socket tracing before launch; observe app and attributed WebView/helper processes through workload/exit with network available and repeat under isolation. Independently run a known-connect positive control outside the app. Oracle: zero app-initiated outbound connections, including loopback; classify OS-only traffic separately. Evidence: PID/process lineage, raw socket/trace records, capture coverage/drop status and positive-control detection.
scenarios.expected: No telemetry, crash upload, font fetch, updater, HTTP listener/client or task transmission is initiated by the production application. Bundled/IPC URLs create no network connection. Polling snapshots alone, failed observation permissions or undetected positive controls cannot establish a pass.

scenarios.description: Fixture: app-managed directory/database/sidecars/diagnostics, two distinct unprivileged OS accounts, one specifically selected backup and unrelated sibling/managed-file hardlink/symlink fixtures. Stimulus: second-account read attempts and native-boundary requests for arbitrary paths, sibling files, aliases and unselected resources. Oracle: current-account managed locations and exact selected-file scope. Evidence: UID-independent permission/ACL records, denied read results and file digests.
scenarios.expected: Managed directories are 0700 and managed files 0600 without broader granting ACLs; the other unprivileged account cannot read them. Selection grants only the selected file and necessary narrow temporary artifacts; managed aliases and arbitrary paths are denied. No protection against same-account hostile processes is claimed.

scenarios.description: Fixture: actual locked embedded engine, independent external acknowledgment ledger and small distinct before/after collection fixtures. Stimulus: six classes create/edit/complete/reopen/delete/whole restore, three deterministic cut points before commit/inside actual pending commit at the qualified turso 0.8.2 WAL File::sync barrier/after observed acknowledgment, twenty SIGKILL trials each (360 total); reopen disk after every kill. Oracle: replay acknowledged operations in admission order, allowing only the one terminal unacknowledged operation wholly absent/present. Evidence: all 360 keyed trial records, checkpoint traces, killed PID, durable external ledger and exact reopened semantic state.
scenarios.expected: Every reopened collection equals an allowed complete sequential history; no lost acknowledgment, partial task fields, mixed restore or unrelated rollback occurs. After acknowledgment the operation is present subject only to later acknowledged supersession. Checkpoint inability/missing trials is unresolved evidence, not a pass.

scenarios.description: Fixture: actual engine with independent A/B snapshots and acknowledged history, including later edits/deletes/restores superseding earlier values. Stimulus: invalid input, genuine transaction/write/commit failure and uncertainty at admitted operation boundaries; discard the UI future and test reconciliation and normal shutdown. Oracle: precomputed complete old/new states and independent ledger, never receipt presence alone. Evidence: failure kind/checkpoint, actual returned acknowledgment/outcome and reopened fields.
scenarios.expected: Known rejection leaves its complete prior state plus unrelated earlier commits. Uncertain outcome remains blocked until reconciled; it is not inferred rollback from an I/O error. A later acknowledged restore/deletion may correctly supersede prior data, and loss of the UI future does not cancel owned commit.

scenarios.description: Fixture: existing valid store/marker/sidecars and disposable copies with read-only access, missing permissions, invalid/corrupt bytes, unsupported future format and partial initialization evidence. Stimulus: launch, retry and attempted mutation. Oracle: pre-run byte digest/length/identity manifest of every existing evidence file. Evidence: denied operations, actionable UI retry/exit and unchanged artifact manifest.
scenarios.expected: Normal modification stops; existing bytes are retained without deletion, empty replacement or downgrade. Startup distinguishes genuine absence from inaccessible/partial-existing evidence. Retry does not authorize repair; restoring access to the valid fixture allows correct loading.

scenarios.description: Fixture: frozen storage-format-1 and backup-format-1 task fixtures, future-version copies and a valid clock-correction record. Stimulus: round-trip current versions and open/restore future versions. Oracle: canonical complete field/identity values and version tags. Evidence: versioned fixture digests and future-version rejections.
scenarios.expected: Initial released formats preserve all field meanings/identities and reject unsupported future versions without modification. Prior-release migration execution is inapplicable only for release one; later formats require prior-fixture upgrade/interruption/failure and retained recovery evidence through a new specification run.

scenarios.description: Fixture: 9,999/10,000/10,001-task fixtures with 200-scalar titles and 10,000-scalar notes, including four-byte scalars, combining sequences, status/date combinations and valid clock correction. Stimulus: restore/create at boundaries, inspect every page (at most 200 summaries per page) and selected full task through GetTask, edit/status change, delete then create, restart and export/restore.
